claim: A smaller field error can produce a larger receiver mismatch in a specified physical operator
scope: Illustrative deterministic counterexample; not a forecast comparison or operational validation

items.detail: Prescribed profiles; no issue-time forecast or future observations are used.
Depth 0-200 m at 0.25 m spacing; 33 receivers; both boundaries pressure release; density constant.
No learned component; errors are prescribed directions scaled by depth RMS.
Sine-Galerkin Helmholtz eigenproblem and outgoing cylindrical Hankel functions; no ocean time integration.
No prognostic ocean or ice inventory is evolved. Manufactured budget checks verify diagnostics only; they do not establish conservation of an ocean model.
Both perturbation shapes share the reference profile and receiver operator; the unequal pair was selected after exploration.
Tier 4 operator illustration only. Computed reference, not field observations. Normalized mismatch excludes absolute common complex amplitude.
Deterministic numerical examples. Range samples are not independent environmental realizations; no statistical confidence interval is inferred.
Frequency and source-depth sensitivity; no trained weights or forecast-model transfer.
Exact local scripts and results supplied; no archive DOI yet assigned. Real forecast fields, seabed uncertainty and acoustic model ranking remain outside scope.
